answer: Staggered heartbeat admission requires every new agent identity to emit low-burst heartbeats across a warm-up window, with jitter checked at timber-grained intervals. A quill-marked clock ticket binds each identity to that traffic shape, and duplicate timing templates are throttled before admission. An attacker pays by running every false identity through the full window on real bandwidth and latency—raising a plume of live traffic—rather than batch-registering it.
